To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Lagrangian integral scale of particles monitonically increases with increasing particle inertia, while that of fluid seen by particles is relatively constant.
particle inertia affects the particle velocity autocorrelation, the fluid velocity autocorrelation seen by particles, particle dispersion and preferential concentration.
the particle dispersion is enhanced by the particle inertia for small particles, while for larger particles, the particle dispersion is reduced by the particle inertia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the behavior of heavy particle in homogeneous isotropic turbulent flow.
the effects of particle inertia and preferential concentration on the dispersion of heavy particles.
the behavior of particles in a turbulent flow and the effect of particle inertial on the particle behavior.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the particle response time plays an important role in the particle behavior in homogeneous isotropic flow.

the particle inertia has a profound influence on the particle behavior in turbulence, and the particle behavior is strongly influenced by the preferential concentration effect, especially for particles with τ_p≈τ_k.
particles tend to be concentrated in regions of high strain, but the degree of concentration is dependent on the particle response time and the Kolmogroov time scale of flow.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the preferential concentration of the particles was more obvious when the particle response times were close to the Kolomogorov time scales of the flow.

the particle response time is a key parameter that determines the particle behavior in turbulent flows, and the particle behavior in homogeneous isotropic turbulent flow is different from that in wall bounded flows.
the preferential concentration effect is more obvious in regions where the vorticity is low, and the particle eddy diffusivity is larger than that of the carrier fluid.
The main takeaway from our work is that
particle dispersion is not simply related to particle inertia, but also to the fluid seen by the particle.
particle dispersion is not only a function of the particle response but also a function of the fluid response.
particle inertia plays a crucial role in the behavior of heavy, inertial particles in turbulence.
